headline: Mechanical models link tissue forces to rheology, cell cycle and wound closure
label: Mechanical Modeling Of Tissues
summary: Recent preprints apply active foam, vertex and data-driven cell-based models to confluent tissue forces, rheology and wound closure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative mechanical modeling of confluent tissues, in which an explicit force or constitutive description is tested against tissue-level observables. One preprint simulates a 2D active foam, comparing traction and junctional-tension forces and reporting universal persistent Brownian long-time cell motion. A second derives mean-field nonlinear rheology for a viscous vertex model and validates it against large-amplitude oscillatory shear. A third fits a data-driven DLCM cell-based model to time-lapse fibroblast data, linking G1 arrest and initial cell-cycle arrangement to wound closure. These items do not share a single mechanism; they share the use of explicit mechanics to generate testable predictions. What is new here is the coupling of cell-cycle state to mechanical wound-closure behavior through data-driven fitting, extending mechanical modeling beyond static rheology and motion statistics.
